prompt: A cylindrical can has radius $3$ in and height $10$ in. Write its exact volume in terms of $\pi$ (for example, write $7\pi$ as 7pi).
hint: A cylinder is a stack of identical circles: $V = \pi r^2 h$.

hints.text: A cylinder is a stack of identical circles: $V = \pi r^2 h$.
The circular base has area $\pi(3)^2 = 9\pi$ square inches.
Multiply by the height: $9\pi \times 10 = 90\pi$ cubic inches.

explanation: Volume is base area times height: $9\pi \times 10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Base times height, always
steps: Every prism and cylinder follows the same rule: area of the base, times how tall it is.
For a box the base is a rectangle; for a can it is a circle. Same idea, different base formula.
